assumptions: The venture remains a no-custody advisory and coordination workflow and does not itself transport, store, test, dismantle, acquire, or handle waste equipment.
Qualified Polish counsel and appropriate insurance can establish a lawful operating boundary without making each work order uneconomic.
Family-installer access is treated only as pilot access, not as evidence of payment, exclusivity, repeat demand, or transferable distribution.
The fixed workflow fee is the conservative revenue event and brokerage revenue is zero unless a compliant professional transfer actually closes.
Competent AI-assisted automation can reduce routine evidence-pack labor but cannot replace legal judgment, physical testing, regulated operations, partner relationships, or exception handling.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: Multiple paid work orders, including repeat use and at least one installer outside the family relationship, showing accepted fixed pricing, full activity-based contribution margin, prompt buyer and authorized-operator quotes, lawful route outcomes, low exception burden, and a quantified advantage over the installer's current process.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: The pre-removal gate targets the point at which title, condition, and documentation can still determine a lawful direct-transfer route, and it makes that route auditable before the equipment becomes a costly handling problem. This is a coherent insight grounded in the regulatory evidence, although the research does not establish that installers experience it as an unmet standalone job rather than part of existing downstream service.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Incorrect classification or incomplete evidence can create compliance exposure, delay, handling cost, and lost residual value, so there is a credible basis for pain. Willingness to pay for a separate checkpoint remains uncertain: no installer has accepted a fee, established operators may already cover enough of the workflow, and the added gate may be perceived as friction rather than avoided cost.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: No custody, no inventory, and a pre-quoted fee independent of resale materially improve capital exposure and cash conversion versus speculative consignment; treating brokerage as zero in the conservative case is disciplined. However, there is no fee, fully loaded service cost, order density, repeat rate, or contribution-margin evidence, while legal review, insurance, partner coordination, and exceptions could consume the margin of a relatively small work-order fee. The path from this service wedge to substantial owner earnings remains unsubstantiated.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Commercial string-inverter replacements in one dense region form a precise, testable beachhead, and the family installer gives bounded access to observe the workflow. The evidence does not establish removal frequency, usable unit volume, buyer demand, or whether this class-region intersection is economically meaningful enough to support a repeatable business.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: An embedded pre-removal decision record could become a useful workflow position if installers mandate it. At present there is no mandate, exclusivity, supply right, or privileged partner access, while PV CYCLE and SecondSol already cover much of the compliance, collection, testing, resale, logistics, and recycling stack. Installers or those incumbents could reproduce the visible process.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A proven inverter workflow could extend to additional installer clusters, equipment classes, counterparties, and geographies, with accumulated route data helping select later adjacencies. Expansion is not automatic because each class and jurisdiction can introduce different testing, product-safety, waste-status, insurance, and authorized-partner requirements.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Serial-level quotes, outcomes, returns, and route records could eventually improve decisions and create workflow switching costs. No proprietary dataset, exclusive supply, contractual workflow right, or partner lock-in exists yet, and the proposed evidence-pack and quote-gate method is readily legible to installers and established downstream operators.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: The no-custody, two-route decision gate offers a meaningful risk and capital improvement over buying or consigning uncertain equipment, while its audit trail may be more reliable than an informal disposal decision. There is no measured improvement in cost, speed, liability reduction, or recovery value versus an installer's current operator relationship, and obtaining two timely quotes may add coordination burden.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: A maturing European PV fleet, increasing waste and reuse activity, and documentation-heavy regulation create a plausible need for better disposition decisions now. The same evidence says second-hand PV guidance is still immature, which increases uncertainty and liability and may delay standardization rather than solely accelerating adoption.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family installer provides a low-cost, founder-accessible route to a bounded pilot, and placing the checkpoint inside an existing work order is more concrete than generic outbound selling. That access is not a paid commitment or transferable channel; repeatable acquisition beyond the family relationship is unknown, and a separate paid step must displace or complement existing downstream-provider routines.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's data and automation skills fit a standardized evidence workflow, and the one-class, no-custody pilot can plausibly be run part-time. Execution still depends on a defensible Polish legal and insurance boundary, accurate classification advice, prompt responses from both professional buyers and authorized operators, dispute allocation, and sufficient local job density; these relationship and liability tasks cannot simply be automated away.

highest_value_structural_change: Turn the optional checkpoint into a contractually embedded white-label work-order module with recurring platform-plus-usage pricing and response-time commitments from authorized operators and professional buyers; this would strengthen the control point, reduce per-order coordination, improve recurring economics, and make the resulting route dataset harder to replicate.
main_structural_strength: Moving the route decision before removal and charging a fixed fee that does not depend on speculative salvage, while leaving all regulated physical work with authorized counterparties, sharply reduces inventory and negative-salvage exposure and permits a bounded founder-accessible pilot.
primary_score_limiter: There is no evidence that installers will authorize and pay enough for this separate checkpoint, at sufficient repeat density, to cover legal, insurance, partner-coordination, and exception costs when established downstream providers may already solve enough of the problem.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: PV CYCLE and SecondSol already provide substantial portions of the proposed downstream compliance, collection, testing, repair, resale, logistics, and recycling stack, directly weakening the claim that this workflow occupies an unserved control point or offers a strong enough advantage to change installer behavior.
